items.title: Highway Breakaway Signs: Why 1,000-Lb Steel Snaps in 50ms
items.description:
Highway breakaway signs hide a violent engineering trick: when hit at seventy miles per hour, why doesn't the steel beam crush your car? In the nineteen sixties, hitting a roadside sign meant colliding with an unyielding steel girder embedded in five feet of solid concrete, cutting vehicles in two. Today, modern highway breakaway signs use slotted slip bases and upper hinge plates to launch a thousand-pound post safely over the roof of your vehicle in under fifty milliseconds. In this episode of Cutaway, we break down the physics of directional friction, crash-tested breakaway mechanisms, and the surprising reason low-speed crashes are sometimes more dangerous than high-speed impacts.
